messages:
alex: Heads-up — p99 for streaming chat spiked after the kernel selector bump (v2->v3). Observed 220ms -> ~420ms on p99 for mb=1.
perf-bot: [auto-trace] span(root) svc=serve runtime_kernel_switch=hotpatch_v3 kv_prefetch=off samples=1200
maya: Is this specifically streaming (chunked) requests or also non-streaming completions?
alex: Streaming chunked chat only. Non-streaming completions (mb=4) stayed around 250-280ms p99.
maya: Interesting. Did the bump change kernel fallback timing or handshake behavior?
cheng: Putting profiler output (trimmed):
```
CPU: kernel_selector: 43%
GPU: kernel_launch_wait: 18%
Runtime: kv_cache_miss_eviction: 11% (taily)
IO: handshake_wait: 9%
```
cheng: Noticed the kernel switch now triggers immediately on first token for streaming; older logic delayed until steady-state.
sam: So for mb=1 we lose warmup batching and we hit more KV misses + kernel cold path -> tail.
raj: Could be kv prefetch disabled in v3? We saw a PR that removed speculative prefetch to avoid memory spikes.
linh: I ran a quick local sweep: `bench/stream --mbsize 1 --kernel v3 --prefetch on/off`
linh: Results (median/p95/p99):
- prefetch=on: 85ms / 190ms / 320ms
- prefetch=off: 90ms / 260ms / 440ms
linh: So prefetch helps tails but doesn't fully recover prior p99.
alex: Thanks — that matches infra traces. Two hypotheses:
1) Immediate kernel switch in v3 causes heavier kernel selection codepath + smaller batch inefficiency
2) Prefetch improvement reduces kv miss cost but kernel cold-launch still hurts p99
maya: Can we test deadline-aware batching? Idea: for streaming if client handshake time > X, hold request for up to 12ms to allow microbatching with others, otherwise stream immediately.
sam: That's basically introduce a small delay budget to trade steady-state latency for tail reduction.
raj: Also consider hysteresis: don't switch kernel for the very first token unless queue is empty for >Y ms.
cheng: I mocked a patch that delays kernel switch by 8ms for streaming when mbsize target=1. Ran a short run:
- no delay: p99 420ms
- delay 8ms: p99 280ms
p95 improved from 210->185ms.
alex: Nice. Any throughput impact?
cheng: negligible at our current qps (1-3k/s). At very high load you'll see throughput drop ~1.5% in synthetic microbench.
linh: Also tried prefetch + delay8ms combo:
- p99 230ms
- p95 170ms
That looks close to old kernel baseline.
maya: Can we add guardrails: only enable delay when observed concurrency < N and client type=chat-streaming? Need to avoid throughput regression on bursty workloads.
sam: Agree. Add config flags: `streaming_deadline_delay_ms`, `kernel_switch_hysteresis_ms`, and an autoswitcher based on short-term RPS.
alex: Quick plan:
- Cheng: land kernel_switch_hysteresis toggle (8ms default) behind feature flag. (owner: cheng)
- Linh: re-enable speculative kv_prefetch behind feature flag and add mem safety cap. (owner: linh)
- Maya: update perf tests to include streaming mb=1 p95/p99 baselines.
- Raj: run cluster canary for 6h with 10% traffic.
cheng: Will post PR later today. Patch includes microbench harness and a flame trace.
linh: I'll run long-run 2h bench for prefetch+delay on a staging pool and share numbers.
sam: Don't forget to update console dashboards: per-route p99, mbsize breakdown and kernel version dimension.
alex: If canary is green, we can roll to 50% and monitor tail-error budgets.
perf-bot: scheduled bench job: job_id=jk-4281, target=staging, tags=[streaming,mb1,kernel-v3,delay8ms]
maya: One more thought — add a small KV warmup for new kernel containers: on first request spin async prefetch of top-k tokens from probed KV keys. Might cut cold-launch tail.
cheng: Yup added to TODO list. If async prefetch can run in parallel with handshake we get better p99 without delaying stream.
alex: Great discussion. Let's keep thread updates limited to short results. Thanks team :thumbsup:
